title: Diagnostic process inspection
intro: Inspection ownership and timing contract. Dark Start here nodes mark graph entry; sequence diagrams begin at their first message. Delivery evidence lives in the diagnostic foundation report.

groups.title: Ownership
groups.description: Keep target signal authority and reaping with one owner.

groups.title: Deadlines
groups.description: An inspection timeout fails evidence while safety actions continue.

groups.title: Helper creation
groups.description: Track helper ownership before exec without making teardown wait.

discussion.title: Keep inspection off the teardown path
discussion.summary: One prestarted read-only worker owns ps creation and waits. One controller scheduler serves workload safety, teardown and worker timers. Group KILL occurs at T without pre-escalation inspection. Helper identity publication precedes exec without a per-helper ACK. A failed worker is retired without replacement. Storage isolation is a separate boundary.

updatedDiagrams.summary: One controller scheduler serves every wait and timer. The worker resets inherited host state.
Group grace has no query. KILL at T precedes the sole final query, whose cutoff lies inside K.
Publication before exec needs no controller ACK. Explicit fork failure differs from unknown creation.

diagrams.title: Keep signals with the controller
diagrams.caption: The worker may signal only its own unreaped direct helper. Both group leaders stay pinned until their group signal authority closes. A teardown command cannot suspend worker timers. Storage isolation has its own contract.

diagrams.title: Expire evidence without delaying safety
diagrams.caption: Group termination waits through grace and attempts KILL at T. This example observes leader exit during grace, then shows a stalled final query. PID-only interruption skips KILL after observed exit. Late leader exit can prevent a final query, and still-exiting members can fail it. R reserves reap time, not ps latency. OS scheduling limits apply.

diagrams.title: Publish before exec
diagrams.caption: The worker publishes identity before gate release. The controller need not receive it before exec. Expiry and epoch validation reject late results. A timely fork error has no helper residual. Missing identity at deadline or worker exit leaves unknown creation. Bootstrap readiness still has its separate ACK.
